phases.name: Element extraction identity and cardinality

tasks.description: Trace Rust impl_item and Java/C++ class-body traversal in ElementExtractor plus its direct tests; success means every double-visit path and required scoped-name behavior is explicitly identified.

HALT FOR OPERATOR RULING before any edit to the Java or C/C++ branch. Rust and C++ emit byte-identical duplicate pairs, so dedup there is unambiguous. JAVA DOES NOT: element-extractor.ts:558 traverses the class body scoped (emitting `Svc.alpha` as type `method`) and the unconditional child loop at :578 re-walks the same body unscoped (emitting `alpha` as type `function`). Removing the second pass therefore DELETES the bare-name element - it is a semantic change, not a dedup. This matters downstream: the phase-2 ticket (TKT-XGZA82) exists because tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:63 reduces qualified method names to bare names before call matching, so whichever identity survives here defines what phase 2 must do. Paths: (A) keep the QUALIFIED `Svc.alpha` method only - matches the TS/Python class-method convention, but any consumer keyed on the bare name loses its match until phase 2 lands; (B) keep the BARE `alpha` function only - preserves current call-matching behavior, but Java classes stop producing methods and diverge from every other language; (C) keep BOTH deliberately, dropping only the exact-duplicate Rust/C++ pairs, and defer the Java identity question to phase 2 where the consumer lives. Record the choice and its rationale in communication.json decisions_log; do not choose unilaterally.

Make the scoped-then-unconditional traversal single-pass at the three confirmed sites: element-extractor.ts:480 (Rust impl_item), :558 (Java class_declaration) and :634 (C++ class_specifier/struct_specifier). Each traverses a scoped body and then re-walks the SAME children via the unconditional loop that follows. SCOPE CORRECTION: do NOT describe this as preserving qualification for Rust - `parentScope` is threaded through extractRustElements and NEVER READ (verified against every reference in the function, lines 451-507), so Rust has no scoped naming to preserve and its duplicates are exact. Introducing Rust scoped names would be NEW behavior and is explicitly OUT of scope for this phase; if wanted, mint it separately. Clone substrate and complexity metadata must survive on the element that is kept. Java and C/C++ follow the P1-T1a ruling.

Add Rust, Java and C/C++ fixtures asserting exact element cardinality and the ruled scoped-name behavior; success means the pre-edit implementation FAILS the new assertions and the corrected one passes. The new cases MUST NOT use the existing `if (!parser) return;` skip pattern - an unloadable grammar has to fail the test, not silently green it. That guard is why this class of bug survived: the current Java cases assert only `expect(elements).toBeDefined()` (element-extractor.test.ts:319, :340) and the C/C++ cases use `.find()`, which returns the first match and is structurally blind to duplicates - all of them pass today WITH the bug present. Note the grammar registry key for Rust is `rs`, not `rust`; getParser("rust") returns undefined with no error and would silently disable the whole Rust case.
Run ElementExtractor, complexity-metrics, clone-substrate, and scanner regression suites; success means all targeted suites exit zero without snapshot or cardinality regressions.

Re-run a quick discovery and inspect emitted element identities before authoring Phase 2; success means duplicate elements are absent and the tree-sitter relationship phase can be planned against stable upstream facts.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1 REPRODUCE FIRST: a fixture-based test asserts the CURRENT duplicate emission and is seen to FAIL only after the P1-T2 edit. Measured 2026-08-01 on HEAD: a Rust `impl Foo` with 2 fns emits 5 elements (alpha, beta, alpha, beta + class); the same C++ class emits 5 (alpha, beta, alpha, beta + class); the same Java class emits 5 (class Svc, method Svc.alpha, method Svc.beta, function alpha, function beta).
AC-2 CARDINALITY: after the edit each of the three fixtures emits exactly one element per declared construct — Rust 3, C++ 3, Java 3.
AC-3 NO SILENT SKIP: every new language assertion FAILS when its grammar is absent. The existing `if (!parser) return;` guard is banned in the new cases.

AC-4 NO TS REGRESSION: the "Phase 1 regression: class_declaration recursion leak" block (element-extractor.test.ts:425) still passes unchanged — the TS path was already fixed for this exact shape and must not be re-broken.
AC-5 IDENTITY RULING RECORDED: the P1-T1a ruling is written into communication.json decisions_log before P1-T2 edits Java or C++.
